topic.title: Fair Prediction and Causal Fairness
topic.overview: Fairness methods examine how predictions differ across groups, which training examples drive those differences, and which uses of sensitive information are acceptable. This cluster includes statistical constraints, reweighting, influence analysis, counterfactual modeling, and fairness–utility tradeoffs. Different definitions encode different choices about the harms a model should avoid.
topic.whyItMatters: A fairness requirement cannot be evaluated independently of the dataset, uncertainty, and intended decision. Quantifying achievable tradeoffs and causal pathways can make disagreements explicit instead of hiding them behind a single disparity score.
topic.evolution: Early representatives address aggregation bias, equal opportunity, and causal discrimination. Later work studies demographic-free reweighting and instance-level interventions. Recent examples estimate dataset-specific fairness frontiers with uncertainty and organize path-specific counterfactual notions into a hierarchy, broadening how fairness claims can be interpreted and compared.
openQuestions: How should uncertainty in a learned causal graph affect fairness conclusions?
Which tradeoffs remain acceptable after deployment changes the population or its behavior?

papers.title: On Group Sufficiency Under Label Bias
papers.tldr: The paper shows how biased labels undermine group calibration and proposes a regularizer that reduces the resulting sufficiency gap.

papers.title: Some Optimizers are More Equal: Understanding the Role of Optimizers in Group Fairness
papers.tldr: Conditional theory and experiments show that adaptive optimizers can improve group fairness relative to SGD while maintaining comparable accuracy.

papers.title: The Boundaries of Fair AI in Medical Image Prognosis: A Causal Perspective
papers.tldr: FairTTE finds widespread bias and limited effectiveness of current fairness methods in medical image prognosis, especially under distribution shifts.

papers.title: Understanding challenges to the interpretation of disaggregated evaluations of algorithmic fairness
papers.tldr: Subgroup performance comparisons can mislead fairness assessments unless their interpretation accounts for real-world disparities, selection bias, and causal assumptions.

papers.title: Understanding Fairness and Prediction Error through Subspace Decomposition and Influence Analysis
papers.tldr: The paper decomposes data representations into predictive, sensitive, and shared components to analyze and manage fairness–accuracy trade-offs.

papers.title: Beyond Procedure: Substantive Fairness in Conformal Prediction
papers.tldr: The paper connects conformal prediction to downstream fairness and finds that equalized prediction-set sizes correlate strongly with fairer outcomes.

papers.title: CELL: A Causal Perspective for Fairness-aware Graph Adaptation
papers.tldr: CELL combines causal factor separation and graph alignment to improve prediction and fairness without target-domain sensitive labels.

papers.title: Correcting Overparameterization Effects in Fair Empirical Risk Minimization
papers.tldr: Allowing calibrated bias overcompensation can correct fairness constraints that fail in the analyzed overparameterized regime.

papers.title: Equalized Generative Treatment: Matching f-divergences for Fairness in Generative Models
papers.tldr: Equalized generative treatment measures fairness through comparable generation quality across groups and motivates min–max fine-tuning to balance that quality.

papers.title: Extending Fair Null-Space Projections for Continuous Attributes to Kernel Methods
papers.tldr: A direct kernel-matrix transformation extends fair null-space projection to continuous protected attributes and shows competitive results with Support Vector Regression.

papers.title: Fair Dataset Distillation via Cross-Group Barycenter Alignment
papers.tldr: Aligning subgroup predictive information during dataset distillation reduces fairness gaps that balancing group sizes alone does not remove.

papers.title: Fair-FedMOE: Group-Fair One-Shot Federated Learning via Prototype-Guided Experts for Medical Imaging Analysis
papers.tldr: Fair-FedMOE uses subgroup experts and prototype-guided aggregation to improve medical imaging fairness in one-shot federated learning without sacrificing reported accuracy.

papers.title: FairMerging: Rethinking Model Merging through the Lens of Fairness
papers.tldr: FairMerging reduces subgroup disparities by addressing model sensitivity and fairness when choosing how to combine task-specific models.

papers.title: HoloFair: Unified T2I Fairness Evaluation and Fair-GRPO Debiasing
papers.tldr: HoloFair evaluates multidimensional demographic bias, while Fair-GRPO improves measured fairness through reinforcement learning with a multi-objective reward.

papers.title: Position: Beyond Sensitive Attributes, ML Fairness Should Quantify Structural Injustice via Social Determinants
papers.tldr: The paper argues that fairness audits should measure structural injustice through social determinants before choosing mitigation strategies.

papers.title: Position: Fairness Failure in Generative Models is an Evaluation Problem
papers.tldr: The paper proposes Fairness Cards to make generative-model fairness evaluations reproducible, comparable, and useful for deployment decisions.

papers.title: Position: Why Current Fair-AI Fails Spatial Fairness, And How to Adapt to It
papers.tldr: Spatial fairness requires treating location as socially consequential data that can carry protected-characteristic biases into sensitive decisions.

papers.title: RAIGen: Rare Attribute Identification in Text-to-Image Generative Models
papers.tldr: RAIGen discovers and helps amplify rare attributes encoded in diffusion models without requiring predefined minority categories.

papers.title: RECAST: Model Reconstruction via Counterfactual-Aware Wasserstein Geometry under Limited Data
papers.tldr: RECAST uses counterfactual-aware Wasserstein prototypes to reconstruct black-box behavior from limited data without online access during reconstruction.

papers.title: The Fairness Hierarchy: A viewpoint from causal inference
papers.tldr: The framework organizes fairness notions by selectively allowing or blocking sensitive-attribute influence along paths in a learned causal graph.
